body.p: This listing of claims is responsive to the Office Action mailed May 10, 2024, which has been carefully considered. Reconsideration and allowance of the subject application are requested for at least the following reasons.

Applicant greatly appreciates the remarks on page 11 of the Office Action indicating that claim 2 is objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim but would be allowable if overcome the 35 USC 112(b) rejection and rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims.
Claims 7-8 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 s being directed to or encompassing a human organism.

While Applicant disagrees with the above rejection, Applicant has amended claim 8 to recite, inter alia, "wherein the system comprises a scattering layer configured to be disposed disposable between the matrix in which the one or more optical fibres of the optical fibre assembly are embedded and the individual."
Applicant respectfully submits that claim 7 recites, inter alia,

Accordingly, claim 7 is not directed to or encompassing a human organism, but rather is clarifying the structure and/or functionality of the one or more optical fibres of the optical fibre assembly relative to the matrix.
Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 101 is therefore respectfully requested.

Claims 1-3, 5-8, 11, 14-15, and 17-18 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor (or for applications subject to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, the applicant), regards as the invention. Claims that depend directly or indirectly from claim(s) 1 and 7 is/are also rejected due to said dependency.
In regard to claim 11, Applicant has amended "an individual" with "the individual."
Reconsideration and withdrawal of the above rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 112 is therefore respectfully requested.

Claims 1, 3, 5-8, and 19-21 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Mannheimer et al. (USPN 8,352,004, hereinafter "Mannheimer") in view of Tjin (USPGPUB 2004/0074307, hereinafter "Tjin") and evidenced by Bartol et al. (USPGPUB 2014/0058288, hereinafter "Bartol"). Claims 11, 14-15, 17-18, and 22-23 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over the combination of Mannheimer and Tjin in further in view of Beska et al. (USPGPUB 2010/0249557, hereinafter "Beska").

While Applicant respectfully disagrees with this rejection, Applicant has amended independent claim 1 to clarify that "the optical fibre assembly is configured to measure the physiological parameter only when contact pressure of the optical fibre assembly measured by the pressure sensor is determined to be within a predefined range."

Upon review, nothing in the cited references teaches or suggests an optical fibre assembly configured to measure a physiological parameter only when contact pressure of the optical fibre assembly, as measured by a pressure sensor, is determined to be within a predefined range.

Applicant notes that in the rejection of claim 20, the Office asserts that FIG. 4 and Col. 5, lines 38-54 of Mannheimer for the features of claim 20. A copy of FIG. 4 and Col. 5, lines 38-54 of Mannheimer is provided below for the Examiner's convenience.

FIG. 4 shows an embodiment of a sensor 1OC with a strain gauge contact sensor 12C. The strain gauge contact sensor 12C may incorporate a conductive grid 52 applied to a carrier matrix 54, for example a semiconductive material, that is capable of relaying a signal related to a pressure level when the sensor 10C is properly applied at a sensing site. In an embodiment, the electrical resistance of the grid may vary linearly with strain, and force or pressure on the strain gauge contact sensor 12C may be determined by measuring the change in resistance. Such a configuration may provide the advantage of relaying more detailed information about the nature of the contact rather than only an on/off signal. A downstream medical device such as a monitor, discussed below, may process the signal in order to characterize the nature of the pressure and determine if the pressure is associated with a "sensor on" or "sensor off' state, among other determinations utilizing the
signal.

Upon review, however, nothing in the cited passage of Mannheimer is understood to teach or suggest that an optical fibre assembly configured to measure a physiological parameter only when contact pressure of the optical fibre assembly, as measured by a pressure sensor, is determined to be within a predefined range as generally recited in amended, independent claim 1.

Applicant further submits that Tjin, Bartol, and Beska do not remedy the above-noted deficiencies of Mannheimer, nor have they been asserted to provide such teachings. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that the above rejections under Mannheimer, Tjin, and Beska may be withdrawn upon reconsideration.

Independent claim 19 has been amended to include, inter alia, features similar to those discussed above with respect to amended, independent claim 1. As such, Applicant respectfully submits that the rejection of amended, independent claim 19 may be withdrawn for at least similar reasons as those discussed above with respect to amended, independent claim 1, and will not be repeated for the sake of brevity.

It is believed that all the pending claims have been addressed. However, the absence of a reply to a specific rejection, issue or comment does not signify agreement with or concession of that rejection, issue or comment. In addition, because the arguments made above may not be exhaustive, there may be reasons for patentability of any or all pending claims (or other claims) that have not been expressed. Finally, nothing in this paper should be construed as intent to concede any issue regarding any claim, except as specifically stated in this paper.

Having dealt with all the objections raised by the Examiner, it is respectfully submitted that the present application, as amended, is in condition for allowance. Thus, early allowance is earnestly solicited.
